Maria — thanks. Quick answers and proposed flow below.

Proration: Redwood will prorate the first partial month (May) based on acceptance date. Example: if you accept on May 15 we invoice 17 days prorated for May. I attached a one-line proration table in the Renewal_Summary.

Marketplace acceptance routing options (choose one):
A) Acme signs PO to Redwood; Redwood submits signed PO + acceptance to AWS Marketplace on your behalf (consolidated billing). We'll need the signed PO and a signed acceptance PDF.
B) Acme accepts the private offer through the AWS Marketplace console directly (you retain the acceptance audit trail).

DocuSign: I can send a DocuSign envelope that contains the PO and the acceptance addendum that Redwood will submit to AWS if you pick option A. If you prefer B, share the email of the user who will accept in the console and we'll provide step-by-step.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/9843 (for internal tracking)
DocuSign draft: https://www.docusign.net/contract/ABC-123-REDWOOD

If procurement confirms monthly invoices, finance will work with our billing team to map the PO to monthly invoice tranches. Otherwise we can accept a single annual invoice.

I'll send the DocuSign packet now as option A is the faster path to get you live on May 1.

Best,
Vanessa

Hi all — quick note from the Marketplace team: if Acme wants consolidated billing via AWS Marketplace (option A), AWS requires the signed PO + acceptance document and a Marketplace-facing email on file. In practice we:

- Send DocuSign to Acme with the PO + acceptance addendum.
- Once signed, we (Redwood) upload the acceptance package to AWS Marketplace support and request the private offer activation.
- AWS has a 48–72 hour processing window to link the private offer to the buyer account.
